title: About Us | New York Auto Transport | Big Apple Car Shipping
metaDescription: Big Apple Car Shipping is a New York–based, FMCSA-licensed auto transport broker with ten local offices from the Bronx and Long Island to Buffalo.
h1: A New York car shipping company, built around the parts other brokers get wrong
heroSub: We started Big Apple Car Shipping because shipping a car out of New York should not require three days of phone calls and a price that changes the night before pickup.
body:
Big Apple Car Shipping is an auto transport broker licensed by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration and based in New York State. We arrange open and enclosed car shipping from anywhere in New York to all fifty states, and from anywhere in the country back to New York. Our dispatch team works out of ten local offices: the Bronx, Yonkers, Hempstead, North Hempstead, Babylon, Islip, Brookhaven, Albany, Schenectady and Buffalo.

What a broker does, and why you want one that knows New York

Almost every car shipped in the United States is moved by a small, independent carrier: a driver who owns one or two trucks and runs a handful of lanes. Brokers like us find the right carrier for your route, vet their authority and insurance, agree the price, and manage the pickup and delivery. The difference between a good broker and a bad one is whether the price you were quoted is a price a real carrier will accept, and whether anyone has thought about how a 75-foot truck gets to your street.

That second part is where being from here matters. Every parkway in the New York metro bans commercial trucks. Half of Manhattan and the Bronx is alternate-side parking. Long Island's canal neighborhoods dead-end at the water, and the Gold Coast's private roads have gates and low branches. Our dispatchers plan pickups around all of that, and they will tell you up front when a meeting point at a station lot or a shopping center is going to work better than your driveway.

How we price

The quote you get from our tool is the all-in price: carrier fee, our fee, fuel, taxes, standard cargo insurance and door-to-door service. We quote at the rate carriers on your lane are actually accepting this week, not a low number designed to win the booking and then creep upward. A small deposit holds your price when a carrier is assigned, and the balance is paid to the driver when your car is delivered and inspected.

How we vet carriers

Before a carrier is assigned to your vehicle we confirm their FMCSA operating authority is active, verify their cargo insurance certificate and limits, and review their safety record and our own history with them. We do this at dispatch, every time, because insurance lapses and authority revocations happen mid-year. If something does not check out, the load goes to someone else.

What you can expect from us

  • An exact price in about a minute, and a human on the phone seven days a week at every office.
  • One coordinator from booking to delivery, with a direct number.
  • A pickup window agreed in advance, and a driver who calls 12 to 24 hours before arriving.
  • An inspection and bill of lading at both ends, with photos we encourage you to take as well.
  • Straight answers when something goes sideways. Trucks break down and weather closes passes; when that happens you will hear it from us first, with a new date.

Who we ship for

Snowbirds heading between Long Island or Westchester and Florida each season. Families relocating to the Carolinas, Georgia, Texas and Arizona. Students at SUNY, CUNY, Hofstra, Stony Brook, UB and Union. Service members moving between Fort Drum, West Point, Fort Hamilton and bases across the country. Collectors on the North Shore and in Scarsdale who ship enclosed. Buyers who found the right car in another state and want it delivered to their door. If it has wheels and a destination, we can probably move it.

Our licensing details and insurance information are on the licensing and insurance page, and every office's address and phone number is on the contact page.

title: Licensing and Insurance | Big Apple Car Shipping
metaDescription: How Big Apple Car Shipping is licensed and bonded, how carrier cargo insurance covers your vehicle in transit, and what to do if there is a claim.
h1: Licensing, bonding and how your car is insured
heroSub: Everything you need to verify that we are licensed, that the carrier moving your car is insured, and what happens in the rare case something goes wrong.
body:
Our federal authority

Big Apple Car Shipping operates as a property broker under authority granted by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), the agency of the U.S. Department of Transportation that regulates interstate trucking.

Legal nameBig Apple Car Shipping
Authority typeProperty broker (auto transport)
Surety bondBMC-84 broker bond, $75,000 (the federal minimum required of every licensed broker)

You can confirm any broker's standing at any time in the FMCSA's public licensing and insurance system (li-public.fmcsa.dot.gov) or the SAFER company snapshot (safer.fmcsa.dot.gov), which show authority status and whether a bond is on file. Our dispatchers will give you our authority details on request when you book. If a company's record shows authority as inactive, do not book with them.

What the broker bond does

The $75,000 surety bond protects the carriers we hire, guaranteeing they are paid for loads they haul for us. It is a condition of our license. It is not vehicle insurance; your car is covered by the carrier's cargo policy, described below.

How your vehicle is insured in transit

From the moment the driver signs the bill of lading at pickup until you sign at delivery, your vehicle is covered by the motor carrier's cargo insurance. Federal rules require every interstate carrier to maintain cargo and liability coverage, and we go further than the minimum:

  • Before any carrier is assigned to your car we obtain and review their current certificate of insurance and confirm their authority is active with FMCSA.
  • Open carriers in our network typically carry cargo limits of $100,000 to $250,000 per load; enclosed carriers typically carry $250,000 to $1,000,000. We match the carrier's limit to the value of what they are hauling.
  • Carrier cargo coverage pays for damage caused by the carrier's negligence during loading, transport and unloading. There is no deductible charged to you for a covered carrier-caused claim.
  • Not covered: personal items left in the vehicle, pre-existing damage noted on the bill of lading, mechanical failures unrelated to transport, and acts of God in most policies. Your own auto policy may provide additional coverage; ask your insurer.

If there is damage

  1. Inspect the car with the driver at delivery, before signing. Compare it to the pickup inspection on the bill of lading.
  2. Note any new damage on the bill of lading, specifically, before you sign. Take photos.
  3. Call your coordinator the same day. We will give you the carrier's insurance information and help you file the claim, and we stay involved until it is resolved.

Damage noted on the delivery bill of lading is the basis of every successful claim. Damage reported after a clean signature is very hard to recover, which is why we ask you not to sign in the dark or in the rain without a proper look.

Our own insurance

In addition to the federal bond, Big Apple Car Shipping carries general liability coverage for its brokerage operations. Certificates are available to commercial customers on request.

Questions about any of this are welcome; call __PHONE_DISPLAY__ or see the contact page for your local office.

title: Privacy Policy | Big Apple Car Shipping
metaDescription: How Big Apple Car Shipping collects, uses and protects the information you provide when you request a quote or book, including SMS messaging consent.
heroSub: Effective October 9, 2026. This policy explains what we collect when you use this website or our services, how we use it, and the choices you have.
body:
Who we are

This website is operated by Big Apple Car Shipping ("we", "us"), an auto transport broker based in New York. Contact details are on the contact page.

Information we collect

  • Information you give us. When you request a quote or book a shipment we collect your name, email address, phone number, pickup and delivery locations, vehicle details, preferred dates and payment information needed to process a deposit.
  • Information collected automatically. Like most websites we receive your IP address, browser type, device information, pages visited and referring URL, through server logs and analytics cookies.
  • Communications. If you call, email or text us we keep a record of the conversation so your coordinator can manage your shipment.

How we use it

  • To price, book, dispatch and deliver your shipment and to communicate with you about it.
  • To share the information a carrier needs to pick up and deliver your vehicle: your name, phone number, addresses and vehicle details.
  • To respond to questions, resolve claims and provide customer support.
  • To send service updates and, if you have agreed, marketing messages. You can opt out at any time.
  • To operate, secure and improve this website.
  • To comply with law and enforce our terms.

SMS and text messaging

By checking the consent box on a quote form you agree to receive recurring SMS messages from Big Apple Car Shipping about your quote and shipment, such as pricing, carrier assignment, pickup and delivery updates. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Consent is not a condition of purchase. Reply STOP to any message to unsubscribe and HELP for assistance, or call __PHONE_DISPLAY__. Mobile phone numbers and SMS consent are never sold, rented or shared with third parties or affiliates for their marketing purposes.

Sharing

We share personal information only with: the motor carrier assigned to your shipment; service providers who process payments, host our systems, send messages or provide analytics on our behalf and under contract; and authorities when required by law. We do not sell personal information.

Cookies and analytics

We use cookies and similar technologies for site functionality and analytics. You can control cookies through your browser settings; disabling them may affect parts of the site, including the quote tool.

Retention and security

We keep shipment records for as long as needed to provide the service, handle claims and meet legal and accounting obligations. We use reasonable administrative, technical and physical safeguards to protect personal information, though no method of transmission or storage is completely secure.

Your choices and rights

You may ask us to access, correct or delete the personal information we hold about you, or to stop marketing communications, by emailing __EMAIL__. Residents of states with consumer privacy laws may have additional rights, which we will honor as the law requires. We do not knowingly collect information from children under 16.

Changes

We may update this policy from time to time. The effective date at the top shows when it was last changed. Continued use of the site after a change means you accept the updated policy.

title: Terms of Service | Big Apple Car Shipping
metaDescription: Terms for quotes and bookings with Big Apple Car Shipping: pricing, deposits, cancellations, pickup windows, inspections, insurance and claims.
heroSub: Effective October 9, 2026. These terms govern quotes and bookings made through this website or by phone with Big Apple Car Shipping.
body:
1. Who we are and what we do

Big Apple Car Shipping ("we") is a licensed property broker. We arrange the transport of your vehicle by independent, FMCSA-licensed and insured motor carriers. We do not own the trucks. The carrier assigned to your shipment is responsible for the physical transport and carries the cargo insurance that covers your vehicle in transit.

2. Quotes and pricing

Quotes are based on the information you provide: route, vehicle year, make and model, whether it runs, trailer type and dates. The quoted price includes carrier transport, our brokerage fee, fuel, taxes, door-to-door service where accessible, and the carrier's standard cargo insurance. Prices may change if the information provided was inaccurate (for example an inoperable vehicle quoted as running, or a vehicle that is modified, oversized or carries additional items), or if you change the route, dates or trailer type after booking. We will tell you about any change before it applies.

3. Booking, deposit and payment

A booking is confirmed when you accept a quote and provide payment details. A deposit is charged when a carrier is assigned to your shipment; the remaining balance is paid directly to the carrier at delivery in the form stated on your confirmation (typically cash, certified funds or an approved electronic method). Payment in full is required before the vehicle is released.

4. Pickup and delivery windows

Pickup dates are windows, not appointments. We will give you an estimated first-available date and a typical window (usually one to five days) and the carrier will call ahead to agree a time. Transit times are estimates based on distance and typical conditions and are not guaranteed. Delays caused by weather, traffic, road closures, mechanical breakdowns, inspections or other events outside our control do not entitle you to compensation beyond any guaranteed-date service you have specifically purchased, whose terms will be stated on your confirmation.

5. Door-to-door service and meeting points

Carriers will get as close to your address as is legal and safe for their equipment. Where a street is restricted to trucks, too narrow, or otherwise inaccessible, you agree to meet the driver at a mutually agreed nearby location such as a large parking lot.

6. Your responsibilities

  • Have the vehicle ready at pickup with no more than a quarter tank of fuel, in the operating condition described at booking, with a working battery and tires, and with any alarm disabled.
  • Remove toll transponders, parking permits, loose or detachable exterior items, and all personal belongings of value. Personal items are shipped at your own risk, are not covered by cargo insurance, and carriers may refuse or charge for excess items.
  • Ensure you or an authorized adult with keys is present at pickup and delivery to sign the bill of lading.
  • Provide accurate contact information and be reachable during the pickup and delivery windows.

7. Inspection, bill of lading and claims

At pickup the driver completes an inspection report on the bill of lading noting the vehicle's condition; please review and sign it. At delivery, inspect the vehicle before signing and note any new damage on the bill of lading. Damage not noted at delivery is presumed not to have occurred in transit. Claims for transit damage are made against the carrier's cargo insurance; we will provide the carrier's insurance information and assist you with the claim. Our liability as a broker is limited to the brokerage fee paid to us.

8. Cancellations

You may cancel at no charge at any time before a carrier is assigned. Once a carrier has been assigned and the deposit charged, cancellations may forfeit the deposit to cover carrier dispatch costs. If we are unable to assign a carrier within a reasonable time of your first available date, you may cancel for a full refund of any amount paid to us.

9. Inoperable, modified and oversized vehicles

Vehicles that do not start, steer, roll and brake require winch loading and are subject to an inoperable surcharge. Lifted, lowered, oversized, dually or heavily loaded vehicles may require special equipment and pricing. Please describe your vehicle accurately at booking.

10. Communications

By providing your phone number and email you agree that we and the assigned carrier may contact you about your shipment by phone, text and email. SMS consent terms are described in our privacy policy; reply STOP to opt out of texts at any time.

11. Limitation of liability

To the fullest extent permitted by law, we are not liable for indirect, incidental or consequential damages, including loss of use, rental cars, missed flights or lost income, arising from delay, damage or any other aspect of the transport service. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law.

12. Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of the State of New York and applicable federal transportation law. Disputes will be brought in the state or federal courts located in New York.

13. Changes

We may update these terms; the version in force when you book applies to that booking. Questions about these terms can be sent to __EMAIL__.
